label.en: Partner's means limit for qualified adult increase tapered withdrawal

description.en: Sets the weekly means (income) limit for a claimant's partner, above which the Qualified Adult Increase (QAI) begins to be tapered down rather than paid in full. It is used as the 'withdraw_start' parameter in BenCalc for the tapered QAI computed in AMtesting_ie (shared logic used by bdict, bhl, bunct, bdinc and bunnc in 2006-07) and directly in bunct_ie, pdi_ie and poact_ie. It applies the general Irish social-welfare rule that once a qualified adult's own weekly means exceed a threshold (€100 in this model), the adult-dependant increase on Jobseeker's Benefit, Invalidity Pension and the State Pension (Contributory) is reduced on a sliding scale rather than paid at the full rate.

description.en: This constant sets the weekly income exemption threshold for the Irish Health Contribution Levy (tschl), the earmarked health-insurance-style social contribution that applied in Ireland from the late 1970s until it was abolished and folded into the Universal Social Charge in 2011. Income at or below this weekly amount is exempt from the levy entirely; it is used in the tschl_ie policy's Elig function (elig_cond parameter) to determine whether an individual is liable for the contribution at all. The constant has 4 historical values starting from 2006-01-01, reflecting periodic upratings of the exemption limit over the levy's final years of operation; the current model version and exact monetary value could not be confirmed from the available theme documentation, which only covers PRSI contributions for 2025-2026 and does not describe this discontinued levy.

According to the theme documentation, the Fuel Allowance means-test income limits differ for those aged under versus at/over this age threshold (e.g. couple and single-person weekly limits change at age 70).

description.en: This constant is the standard weekly Fuel Allowance payment amount (€33 per week in the latest value shown), representing the core cash benefit paid to eligible households during the Fuel Season. It is used in bfua2_ie/BenCalc via the Comp_perTU parameter, meaning it is paid once per qualifying tax/benefit unit (household), consistent with the Country Report's statement that only one Fuel Allowance is paid per household even if multiple members would independently qualify. The theme documentation confirms the weekly rate of €33 (2025) applies during the fuel season, which runs for a fixed number of weeks each winter.

description.en: This constant represents the amount of the Fuel Allowance lump-sum payment option, expressed on a yearly basis (raw value '0#y', latest = 0), reflecting that Ireland allows the Fuel Allowance to be paid either weekly or as two lump sums instead of the weekly rate. It is used in bfua2_ie/BenCalc's Comp_perTU parameter with comment 'FA lump sum', i.e. as an alternative per-tax-unit compensation amount to the weekly rate constant ($bfua2_amt). The theme documentation notes the benefit can be paid 'weekly, or if preferred, in two lump sum amounts' (e.g. two lump sums of €462 in 2025), though in this dataset the modelled lump-sum value is currently zero, likely because the model defaults to simulating the weekly payment mode.

This matches the theme documentation's stated couple income limit for the age >=66/70 band (€1024 in 2025, rising to €1048 in 2026), consistent with the Country Report's note that individuals aged 70 and over face a higher income limit (€1024/week for couples in the cited example year) than younger claimants.

description.en: This is the weekly Fuel Allowance amount paid to an eligible household to help cover heating costs during the winter fuel season. Its current value of €33 matches the pre-2026 weekly Fuel Allowance rate documented for the related bfua2_ie scheme in the benefits theme description (paid weekly for the fuel season, or as two lump sums), before the rate was raised to €38 from 2026; the four historical values recorded since 2006-01-01 track successive upratings of this weekly rate.

description.en: This constant is a numeric parameter (currently €120) feeding into the Comp_Cond formula of bfua_ie/BenCalc, whose function comment is 'Means test for contributory payments' — i.e. it is used when testing eligibility for claimants who qualify via a contributory payment such as State Pension (Contributory), Invalidity Pension or a contributory Widow's/Widower's Pension. The Country Report explains that the Fuel Allowance means test for such claimants is linked to the maximum rate of the State Pension (Contributory), allowing combined weekly income up to a set margin above that maximum rate; $bfua_form_amt most likely represents that income margin/disregard (or another additive component) built into the means-test formula. Because neither source states the parameter's exact economic meaning by name, this description is inferred mainly from the constant's name, its usage site, and the general means-test description; confidence is therefore limited.

The benefits theme table shows qualified-adult increases for contributory pensions in a similar range (e.g. €162-€268.40 depending on age and year), consistent with this constant's magnitude, though the exact figure is not separately documented, so confidence is moderate.

description.en: This constant sets the per-account (tax unit) amount of Ireland's Electricity/Energy Credit, a one-off, universal, non-means-tested lump-sum credit deducted directly from domestic electricity bills, paid to all domestic energy account holders who are not on a low-usage account. It is used in the benergy_cred_ie policy's BenCalc function as the Comp_perTU parameter, i.e. the credit is computed and awarded once per tax unit (household energy account) rather than per person. The latest value is €125, consistent with the one-off €125 instalment paid in January 2025 described in the Country Report and benefits documentation; earlier years saw larger total support (e.g. €250 paid in two €125 instalments across late 2024/early 2025) reflecting the temporary cost-of-living measures introduced from Budget 2023 (first announced/paid in 2022), which the sources note were discontinued from 2026. The credit is exempt from tax and social insurance contributions and is fully simulated in EUROMOD.

description.en: Represents the tax-incidence (theta) weighting parameter for COICOP consumption sub-category 01162 - fresh, chilled or frozen bananas, within the Food and non-alcoholic beverages division. It is one of a large set of $theta_XXXXX constants defined in the Irish tax spine (tco_ie) and consumed by the CT_XBASE indirect-tax add-on, where it is read via the RegExp_Def parameter of the LIST_ct DefIl function to allocate household expenditure/consumption tax incidence across detailed COICOP categories. No current value is set for this constant in the base Irish system (value is 'n/a' from 2006), so it functions as a placeholder/classification parameter that is populated only when the consumption-tax incidence add-on is actually run with expenditure survey data; it is not an income-tax or benefit parameter and carries no independent policy meaning outside that add-on.

description.en: Maximum weekly rate (EUR 229.50, effective from 2024) of the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy for the youngest age band (children under 1 year, equivalent to EUR 5.10/hour for 45 hours). In policy xcc_ie it is used as the Comp_UpLim of a BenCalc component, capping the tapered subsidy amount computed for that age group before it feeds into the childcare-related benefit variable bccfc_s. This corresponds to the NCS income-assessed subsidy described in the theme documentation, which declines linearly from this maximum as household income rises from the lower to the upper income threshold.

classification.reason: Maximum childcare benefit amount set by legislation

description.en: Maximum weekly rate (EUR 195.75, effective from 2024) of the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy for children aged 1 to 3 years (equivalent to EUR 4.35/hour for 45 hours). Used in policy xcc_ie as the Comp_UpLim of a BenCalc component, capping the subsidy amount for that age group as computed towards bccfc_s. It matches the maximum weekly rate for this age band described in the theme documentation on the National Childcare Scheme.

classification.reason: Maximum childcare benefit amount set by legislation

description.en: Maximum weekly rate (EUR 177.75, effective from 2024) of the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy for children aged 3 to 6 years (equivalent to EUR 3.95/hour for 45 hours). Used in policy xcc_ie as the Comp_UpLim of a BenCalc component, capping the subsidy amount for that age group before it is added to bccfc_s. It corresponds to the maximum weekly rate for the oldest of the three age bands described in the theme documentation, though the documentation also notes that the EUROMOD-HHoT implementation effectively only uses the under-1 and 1-3 age groups for childcare cost modelling.

classification.reason: Benefit maximum amount set by government policy

description.en: Minimum weekly floor (EUR 63, effective from 2024) below which the income-assessed National Childcare Scheme (NCS) subsidy cannot fall, used in policy xcc_ie as the Comp_LowLim of a BenCalc component computing bccfc_s. Structurally this floor corresponds to the universal (non-means-tested) NCS subsidy rate, which the theme documentation reports as EUR 96.30/week (EUR 2.14/hour x 45 hours) for 2025 -- the lower 2024 value of EUR 63 implies an earlier, lower universal hourly rate (about EUR 1.40/hour) before the rate was raised.

classification.reason: Benefit minimum amount set by government policy

description.en: Lower annual household disposable income threshold (EUR 26,000, effective from 2024) below which the National Childcare Scheme (NCS) income-assessed subsidy is paid at its maximum age-specific rate. Referenced within the Comp_perElig formula of the BenCalc computing the childcare-related benefit bccfc_s in policy xcc_ie; the theme documentation describes the income-assessed subsidy rate as declining linearly for income between this lower threshold and the upper threshold (EUR 60,000), converging to the universal subsidy floor. The documentation also notes a parametric reform raising this threshold to EUR 34,000 from September 2026.

classification.reason: Income threshold for benefit eligibility/calculation

description.en: Upper annual household disposable income threshold (EUR 60,000, effective from 2024) above which households receive only the universal (non-means-tested) National Childcare Scheme subsidy rather than the higher income-assessed rate. Referenced within the Comp_perElig formula of the BenCalc computing bccfc_s in policy xcc_ie, marking the point where the income-assessed subsidy taper reaches its floor. The theme documentation confirms this EUR 60,000 ceiling for 2025 and notes a planned rise to EUR 68,000 from September 2026.

classification.reason: Income threshold for benefit eligibility/calculation

description.en: Flat weekly gross childcare fee (EUR 190, effective from 2024) charged for full-time centre-based childcare for a child, before any subsidies or discounts. Used in policy xcc_ie as the Comp_perElig formula input of a BenCalc component producing the gross childcare cost variable xcc_s, which is annualised and deducted from disposable income via the adjusted disposable income concept (ils_dispycc). The theme documentation identifies this as the national median weekly fee for the 2022-23 school year, assumed unchanged due to the Core Funding fee freeze covering most providers.

classification.reason: Benefit amount set by government policy

description.en: Fixed weekly discount (EUR 64.50, effective from 2024) representing the value of the free Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) provision (15 hours/week) for eligible children aged 3-5. Used in policy xcc_ie as the Comp_perElig formula input of a BenCalc component producing xccdc_s, modelled as a negative childcare cost that is added back into adjusted disposable income (ils_dispycc), partially offsetting the gross childcare fee (xcc_amt). The theme documentation confirms this amount and notes it is annualised over 52 weeks in line with OECD TaxBEN conventions, even though ECCE formally runs only during the school year.
